cohort: 395 nulliparous women with singleton pregnancies at ≥38 weeks of gestation
finding: Elective cesarean delivery and induction of labor had similar rates of composite maternal morbidity, but elective cesarean delivery was associated with a lower risk of composite neonatal morbidity.
mod_finding: Elective cesarean delivery had similar rates of complications related to composite maternal morbidity compared with induction of labor, but had a lower risk of complications related to composite neonatal morbidity.
birth_weight: Neonatal birth weight was recorded but specific values not provided
